business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) Battery Packs

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental law; Code civil, Code de commerce, Code monétaire et financier; unitary national legal system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Protection Agreement (signed 26 November 2007, in force)
France–China Double Tax Agreement (30 May 1984, as amended by Protocol of 26 November 2013)
France–United States Income Tax Treaty (31 August 1994, as amended by 2009 and 2013 Protocols)
France–Japan Income Tax Treaty (1995, as amended by 2007 and 2013 Protocols)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally in force)
Energy Charter Treaty (ECT — covers energy-storage value chain; France notified withdrawal under EU-coordinated exit, with 20-year survival clause for qualifying investments)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework Pillar Two domestic implementation (Loi n° 2024-364) applicable to multinational groups meeting consolidated revenue thresholds

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-51 and R. 561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier – CMF), transposing EU AML Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and the EU AML Package including Regulation (EU) 2024/1624; Article L. 561-46 CMF and Décret n° 2017-1094 on the French beneficial-owner (UBO) register maintained with the RCS; Articles L. 223-1 et seq. and R. 123-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code (SARL formation and RCS registration); LOI PACTE n° 2019-486 (company law modernization); TRACFIN supervisory framework (Articles L. 561-23 to L. 561-29 CMF); EU restrictive-measures framework (EU Regulations 2580/2001, 881/2002, 269/2014, 833/2014 and related Annexes) and national asset-freeze orders issued by the Minister of Economy with DG Trésor notification; EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 applicable to the LFP battery-pack activity.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the French UBO register is not freely public; access is granted to TRACFIN and supervisory authorities, to bank/notary/registered intermediaries bound by professional secrecy, and to private persons only by court order upon proof of a legitimate interest (per CJEU C-37/20 WM v Sovim); the register name, nationality, birth date, address and percentage of control of each UBO are captured in the non-public RCS file.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / registration extract of the direct corporate shareholder (extrait d'immatriculation or equivalent from the Company Registry of the origin State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial/trade registry of the origin country (e.g., Companies House, SEC, Chamber of Commerce)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) if the origin State is a Contracting Party; otherwise Consular Legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate of the origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the corporate shareholder approving the incorporation of the French SARL and the appointment of the manager (gérant) and representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / corporate secretary of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Convention State); certified sworn translation into French attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (procuration) granted to the local incorporation representative and/or the nominated gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the origin country or French notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed abroad; notarial certification for domestic execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire bulletin n° 3 or foreign judicial-records equivalent) for each gérant and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Service du casier judiciaire national (France) or competent judicial-records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign certificates; sworn French translation required for non-French documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport / national identity card and recent proof of residential address of each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority of the origin country plus notarized certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the notarized copies; sworn French translation of non-French supporting evidence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and certificate of share-capital blocking (attestation de dépôt des fonds / certificat du dépositaire) issued by the French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French licensed credit institution or CDC where the share capital is deposited
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and apostille not required for domestic bank certificates; foreign bank letters require apostille and sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before incorporation and repeated at registration: (1) every UBO, gérant and authorized signatory is screened against the consolidated EU sanctions lists (UN/EU origin: EU Reg. 269/2014, 833/2014, 2580/2001, 881/2002 and Annexes), the Bank of France/DG Trésor national asset-freeze orders, and the OFAC SDN list because the target payment rails include USD-attached Swift LC and TT Wire; (2) mandatory politically-exposed-person (PEP) classification under Article L. 561-10 CMF covering heads of State, senior officials, judges, military officers and their family/close associates present in the UBO chain, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification (Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier per the composite key); (3) adverse-media and negative-news search on each beneficial owner; (4) verification of absence of convictions, bankruptcies and disqualifications for managers (attestations d'honorabilité); (5) all screening evidence is retained in the AML/CTF file for at least five years after incorporation and must be produced to TRACFIN and supervisory bodies on request; (6) the incorporation bank, notary and domiciliation company each perform independent KYC/CDD, so the corporate counsel must consolidate and reconcile the screening results before filing the statutory UBO declaration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI (https://procedures.inpi.fr); name-availability search and collision screening via INPI data repository (https://data.inpi.fr) and the Répertoire National des Sociétés / Infogreffe (RCS records of the competent greffe du tribunal de commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL corporate name must be written in Latin alphabetic script, unique within the RCS and not confusingly similar to existing company names or prior trademarks (Articles L. 711-1 et seq. Code de la propriété intellectuelle); a foreign-language denomination is admissible provided a French translation is furnished for the RCS certificate; non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into Latin characters with the official transliteration certified by a sworn translator; the name must not mislead as to corporate activity, must not violate ordre public or bonnes moeurs, and must not reproduce protected emblems or geographical indications without authorization; the legal form 'SARL' may be appended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ÉTABLISSEMENT DE PAIEMENT / MONNAIE ÉLECTRONIQUE (ACPR licensing required)
PRESTATAIRE DE SERVICES D'INVESTISSEMENT / GESTION DE PORTEFEUILLE (ACPR/AMF licensing required)
MINISTÈRE / PRÉFECTURE / MAIRIE / POLICE / GENDARMERIE / COMMISSARIAT (official public-function tokens, prohibited for private companies)
RÉPUBLIQUE / ÉTAT / CROIX-ROUGE / RED CROSS / CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE (protected emblem and public-law expressions requiring specific authorization)
FRANCE (sensitive national denomination; acceptable only where the corporate purpose or territorial anchoring justifies the usage and the name is not likely to mislead consumers)
LFP / LITHIUM / BATTERIE (not statutorily prohibited, but subject to trademark collision screening in Class 9/12/35 of the INPI register and EUIPO)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Guichet unique or the Greffe rejects the proposed name, the applicant may: (i) file a fresh amended name application within the 30-day reservation window or immediately, with no statutory waiting period; (ii) request reconsideration from the juge commis à la surveillance du registre (supervisory registrar judge) of the Tribunal de commerce within 15 days of the refusal notification, citing Articles R. 123-27 and R. 123-28 of the Commercial Code and showing a prima facie right to the name (prior RCS registration, trademark certificate, or absence of confusion); (iii) where refusal arises from third-party trademark rights, pursue opposition/cancellation before the INPI or the Tribunal judiciaire rather than the administrative channel; (iv) seek urgent interim relief (référé) before the President of the competent court in case of wrongful blockage; the file must include a French due-diligence report evidencing the name search in the RCS, INPI and EUIPO databases.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: under Article L. 123-11-1 et seq. of the Commercial Code the registered office may be domiciled at an approved commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for a maximum of 25 years under a written domiciliation contract; however, for the ISIC 2720 battery-pack manufacturing scope, a virtual office is NOT acceptable as the sole commercial substance because the operating licence (ICPE / Environmental Code) and the établissement principal require a physical industrial site at which DREAL and labour authorities may inspect; the recommended structure is a physical or domiciled registered office in Paris or a major industrial region (e.g., Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, Hauts-de-France) plus a leased production facility for the LFP battery-pack assembly line; a pure virtual seat without industrial premises would jeopardize the operating licence, tax substance and customs status of the entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH (65–80% annual probability) of unannounced on-site inspection of the industrial establishment by DREAL, the labour inspectorate and URSSAF once operations commence; MEDIUM–HIGH (25–35% annual probability) of verification visit at the registered office by the Greffe, tax administration or domiciliation company; during the pre-incorporation stage, the licensing authority normally performs a pre-operational site visit before delivering the ICPE authorization or registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet unique statutory administrative e-filing fee (single-window incorporation dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff per Décret n° 2021-1054 and Articles R. 123-1 et seq. Code de commerce; INPI published schedule 2024 (€24.00 base fee plus optional services).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and incorporation filing fee at the greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (registry clerk)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed regulatory tariff per Arrêté du 28 juillet 2016 (Annexe A. 743-2 Code de commerce), approximately €50 excl. VAT.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory legal announcement (annonce légale) in an authorized journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal gazette of the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Maximum regulated per-line tariff set by Décret n° 2008-1209 (annual order); Paris average €215–€250 including tax for a standard SARL insertion.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation into French of incorporation documents, UBO identity proofs and corporate resolutions (estimated 6–8 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) listed with a Cour d'appel or the French consular network
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional tariff benchmark €50–€75 per page in Paris and major courts; volume discounts applicable for the bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille certification of 2–3 foreign public documents (corporate resolutions, POA, criminal records)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin under the 1961 Hague Convention (for France: Cour d'appel or Ministère des Affaires étrangères)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed State tariff per apostille, average €30–€70 depending on the issuing State; 2.5 documents × €50 benchmark applied.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting of French statuts (articles of association) and authentication of foreign proxy where notarial form is chosen
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial fee for SARL statutes and POA authentication, benchmark €500 excl. tax; notarial form is optional for SARL except where in-kind contributions of real estate or registered IP exceed legal thresholds.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration preparation and lodging (Annexe règlementaire under Article L. 561-46 CMF, Décret n° 2017-1094)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Guichet unique (declaration attached to the RCS registration file)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee included in the INPI/registry tariff; legal drafting covered under the corporate counsel package; UBO-register statutory filing fee €25 ± VAT.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation contract with an approved domiciliation company, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Société de domiciliation registered under Article L. 123-11-2 Code de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark €300–€500 per year for a commercial seat in Paris or a major business district; the domiciliation contract must permit access by authorities and meet Commercial Code substance criteria.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT, PEP, OFAC, UN/EU sanctions and negative-news screening of all UBOs and managers (Enhanced KYC package)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML/CFT compliance consultancy or licensed professional firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional market rate €100–€150 per hour for enhanced KYC/UBO investigation; package estimate 6–8 hours including PEP determination, list screening and consolidated AML report.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Criminal-record certificates and integrity declarations for each gérant and UBO (bulletin n° 3 casier judiciaire or foreign equivalent with apostille)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Service du casier judiciaire national (French Ministry of Justice) and competent records office of the country of residence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: free in France; foreign administrative fees vary from $0 to $80 per certificate; benchmark $30–$50 per document including apostille and incidental courier costs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank share-capital blocking and issuance of the certificate of deposit (certificat du dépositaire des fonds) on a blocked account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French licensed bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee for capital blocking and certification service under Article R. 223-2 Code de commerce; market range €120–€200 as a one-off fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ICPE / Environmental Code operating-licence pre-screening and pre-qualification for LFP battery-pack assembly (rubric 4735 and EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Environmental-law attorney and accredited ICPE engineering consultant (future DREAL filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark $1,500–$2,000 for legal-technical pre-qualification, classifying the activity (déclaration/enregistrement), drafting the preliminary compliance memo and assessing battery waste and safety obligations; 6–10 hours at $160–$250 per hour.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation industrial-site due diligence (lease review, zoning, infrastructure readiness for the production facility)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial scale for lease due diligence and registered-office advice on industrial leases in major French industrial zones; benchmark $800–$1,500 per site.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: State/municipal pre-consultation and authorization liaison for the commercial establishment (déclaration préalable, urbanisme/ICPE information)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipality, DREAL and authorized filing agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consultancy and drafting fees for administrative correspondence and urbanism declarations; State filing taxes excluded from this estimate; market rate $150–$250 per hour.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reservation and trademark-clearance search on the proposed name and brand across RCS, INPI, EUIPO and WIPO databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory search fee for official databases plus professional search-and-opinion fee; European trademark office fees excluded; benchmark $150–$220 for a Class 9/35/37 search package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reserved contingency for exchange-rate variance, re-filings and courier/translation amendments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Reserved (internal governance buffer, not a third-party disbursement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: 10% contingency on the above cost base to absorb EUR/USD movement, possible registry re-filing fees and additional apostille copies during the 90-day document validity window.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (formation and management of SARL), and Articles R. 223-1 to R. 223-11 (registration formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Infogreffe national portal and local Commercial Court Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 form (DEMATET / Déclaration de création d'entreprise) together with the executed Articles of Association (statuts) and supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital is required for SARL; however, at least 10% of the subscribed capital must be paid up in cash on incorporation and placed in a bank deposit or notary custody account until registration. Contributions in kind must be fully paid up and appraised.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously by the shareholders, that: (i) the attached Articles of Association and all subscription lists are approved and adopted as the founding charter of the SARL; (ii) the subscribed share capital is fully allotted as set forth in the subscription list; (iii) the registered office is fixed at [address], subject to later transfer by qualified shareholder decision; (iv) [Name] is appointed as sole gérant for an indefinite period under the terms of the Articles, with powers to bind the company within the corporate purpose; (v) the gérant is authorized to deposit capital, publish legal notices, complete all registry filings, and execute ancillary instruments and formalities required for incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire (mandatory for contributions in kind or if the statutory articles are actes notariés) or the founding shareholders acting jointly.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the written French-language Articles of Association containing all mandatory SAS/SARL clauses: legal form, duration, name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, share allocation, management structure, decision rules, and profit distribution. Execute the articles by all shareholders; if non-notarial, ensure controlled written signatures. Attach a certificate or valuation report for any in-kind contribution.
required_dossiers: Complete draft of Articles of Association in French
Copy of valid government-issued ID or passport for each shareholder
Lease agreement or registered domiciliation contract for the intended head office
Valuation report for non-cash contributions (rapport du commissaire aux apports) if applicable
Draft shareholder/subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the articles, amend the affected clauses in a written avenant, obtain re-execution by all shareholders, and resubmit the corrected statutory package without restarting the full process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Initial Share Capital and Issue of Certificate of Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French commercial bank or a notary public (deposit in a blocked account in the company's name).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the subscribed capital (at least 10% of the nominal cash portion, or 100% of in-kind contributions) into the designated SARL-in-formation account, indicating the corporate purpose and names of contributories. Obtain the 'certificate de dépôt des fonds' issued by the financial institution or notaire verifying the deposit amount and the intended beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Original or certified copy of the Articles of Association
Shareholders' identification and signature specifications
Bank wire or cash deposit acknowledgement referencing the company name
Completed identification / anti-money laundering questionnaire for each funder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or the certificate is defective, resolve AML/KYC documentation gaps, restart with a different regulated bank, or have a notaire hold the funds and reissue a corrected certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Incorporation Notice in a French Legal Gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales – JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal newspaper (JAL) in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, typically accessed via the official Infogreffe or notarial hub.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an incorporation notice containing the SARL's legal form, corporate name, social object, registered office, amount of share capital, names and addresses of managers, and company identification references. Pay the publication fee and obtain the attestation de parution (legal notice proof).
required_dossiers: Finalized Articles of Association excerpt
Identity and authorization of the gérant or notaire submitting the notice
Registration number or planned RCS number if already available
Contact address and email for the registry liaison
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL publishes an erroneous notice, request immediate corrected publication with the same timestamp validity; re-file a corrected notice within 10 days and submit an explanatory letter to the Greffe upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (through the Infogreffe online filing service).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the M0 form (electronic or paper), attach the executed Articles of Association, proof of capital deposit, legal notice attestation, lease or domiciliation proof, and identity/governance statements. Pay the court registry fees automatically online. Upon validation, the Greffe issues the official Kbis extract and assigns SIREN and SIRET numbers; the company then receives its legal personality.
required_dossiers: Signed M0 form (déclaration de création d'entreprise)
Two true copies of the Articles of Association (one for court annex), including statutory annexations
Certificate of capital deposit (from bank or notaire)
Attestation du journal d'annonces légales (legal notice proof)
Lease deed or domiciliation registration in the company's name
Identity documents of the gérant and subscribing shareholders
Declaration of non-conviction and effective management statement (P0/justificatif d'activité)
Consent of the official/representative for using a domiciliation address if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues an 'observation' or rejection, respond within the one-month remediable period by rectifying the defective documents, paying any complementary fee, and refiling via Infogreffe; urgent remedy is a direct visit to the registry desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Social and Fiscal Formalities for Operational Start-Up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF (social security registration), Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) / tax administration, and the corporate register for bench employer status.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one week of Kbis receipt, declare the actual management structure to URSSAF to obtain the company's social affiliation number and register any employee tax arrangements. Request VAT registration and tax directe codes from the SIE if not automatically integrated. Open a permanent corporate bank account and provide the Kbis extract to external counterparties.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract (official registration certificate)
Identity and position of appointed officer
Company bank account numbers and corporate financial references
GUI or simplified environmental attachment form if required under ICPE
Completed employer declarations for personnel hiring (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or the tax office indicates incomplete data, respond through the official teleprocedure (e.g., InfoFCE interface), provide transmitted company identifiers, and correct missing managerial or employer declarations within the statutory deadline to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement) – Service des installations classées, within the Ministry for Ecological Transition.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enregistrement or Autorisation d'Exploitation ICPE for battery pack assembly under the French Rubrique 2530 (Installations de production de piles et accumulateurs), or an Exemption if production capacity is below thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Inspection des Installations Classées (DREAL), in coordination with the French Agency for Environment and Energy Management (ADEME) for technical standards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Battery pack assembly (lithium iron phosphate) is typically classified under ICPE 'Enregistrement' (Tier 3) for installations producing more than 10 tonnes of finished batteries per year; a full public EIA is required only for capacity above 100 tonnes per year, while smaller pilot or lab-scale assembly may be exempt from formal EIA and subject only to declaration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with French Ministerial Orders of 02/02/1998 and 11/09/1980 (COD, pH, suspended matter, heavy metals incl. iron, nickel, cobalt, phosphate and lithium). VOC emissions from NMP or electrolyte solvents must respect the EU Solvent Emissions Directive (2010/75/EU) and the French annual Permissible Emission Limit of 50 mg/Nm³ for non-halogenated VOC; hazardous waste (spent cathode materials, electrolyte residue) must be stored in sealed leak-proof containers and consigned only to licensed removal facilities under the French waste code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before commissioning, the site must obtain: (1) fire safety approval from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) or the Joint Safety Commission for pickling/retail buildings, including compliance with fire-resistance ratings and lithium battery fire suppression; (2) structural load certification confirming floor capacity for loaded palletized cells and racking systems; (3) occupational risk assessment with PSE (Plan de Sécurité Établissement) or a non-classified installations occupational attestation, including charging area ventilation, emergency battery quenching, no-smoking rules, and personal protective equipment for lithium electrolyte exposure; (4) electrical installation conformity certification by an accredited bureau (e.g., Qualifelec via IRYS) and official commissioning notice to the Labour Inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), accessible via impots.gouv.fr; non-resident and foreign-enterprise VAT registration is handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) within DGFiP. Customs export clearance and customs audit sit with the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), accessible via douane.gouv.fr. Corporate formation and the statutory one-stop-shop are administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL must complete company incorporation through the INPI one-stop-shop, obtaining the SIREN and SIRET numbers. DGFiP then attributes the French intra-Community VAT number in the standard national format: FR + two-digit automated key + nine-digit SIREN, i.e. a 13-character VAT identification number. A non-established foreign entity without a French permanent establishment must file a dedicated VAT registration application with DGFiP/SIEE, supply constitutional documents, proof of foreign tax registration, board authorization and a fiscal power of attorney, and, if established outside the EU, appoint an accredited French VAT tax representative before it can obtain an FR VAT number. Processing normally takes 15 to 30 working days from a complete dossier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification. An ordinary non-family SARL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying 'SARL de famille' whose members are natural persons within the statutory family circle is treated by default as a partnership for income tax purposes unless it elects corporate income tax under Article 239 bis AA of the Code général des impôts. French groups may also elect tax consolidation under Article 223 A CGI. Hybrid mismatch outcomes stemming from incompatible foreign entity classifications are addressed through statutory anti-hybrid and controlled-company provisions, principally Articles 209 B and 212 bis CGI, rather than elective pass-through classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for a French-established taxable person performing taxable supplies; France has no general economic turnover registration deferral. The micro-business VAT franchise (franchise en base de TVA) under Article 293 B CGI, with current de minimis turnover limits around EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services, allows small businesses to remain outside the VAT system, but a battery-pack manufacturing exporter cannot rely on that franchise because it must recover input VAT and issue export or intra-Community zero-rated invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is rolling out the Réforme de la Facturation Électronique. Structured e-invoicing under EN 16931 becomes compulsory for domestic B2B transactions: all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026; large and mid-size enterprises must issue e-invoices from that same date; small and micro enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2027. Registered partner dematerialization platforms (PDPs) and the Public Invoicing Portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) receive transaction and e-reporting data using standardized XML/JSON API connections. France does not currently impose real-time fiscal pre-clearance or digital stamping; sanctions apply for non-compliant e-invoicing, and DGFiP audit surveillance uses the FEC electronic accounting file and AI analytics.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4/LFP) battery packs exported from France to a customer established outside the EU are zero-rated as export transactions under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU and the French supplier retains contemporaneous customs, transport and commercial evidence. Intra-EU deliveries to a VAT-registered EU customer are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI subject to a valid customer VAT ID validated on VIES, issuance of the French EC sales list, and proof of transport between Member States. Pure offshore services or services rendered by the French SARL to foreign counterparties and not effectively used in France are placed outside the scope of French VAT or shifted to the customer under reverse-charge rules; the supplier must evidence the customer's place of establishment and the absence of a French economic nexus.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane/DAU) with the registered MRN issued by DGDDI
Bill of Lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or equivalent carrier documentation proving physical departure from France and the EU
Commercial invoice, purchase order, contract, packing list and Incoterms clause
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent export-proceeds bank evidence, including SWIFT MT103 or wire transfer receipt, proving payment reached the French SARL bank account
Customer's VAT identification for intra-Community supply validated via VIES, or foreign business-tax evidence for non-EU buyers
Shipping manifests, container tracking records and, where relevant, customs release data applicable to dangerous-goods consignments such as high-capacity battery packs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If DGFiP audit rejects the export zero-rating evidence, the transaction is reclassified as a taxable domestic supply and output VAT at 20% is assessed, together with statutory late-payment interest (intérêt de retard), a 40% penalty for deliberate misconduct (manquement délibéré) and an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses). DGFiP may retrospectively claw back input VAT recovered on finished battery cells, components, raw materials and subcontracting where the deduction chain is invalidated by the recharacterization. The extended ten-year limitation period applies to concealed or disguised activity, and DGDDI and French criminal courts may additionally prosecute false export declarations or false evidence, exposing corporate representatives to customs fines up to twice the value of the goods and imprisonment in cases of organized export fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), acting with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) as the national foreign-exchange and investment authority, and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the licensing and supervisory banking regulator under Title I, Livre V of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France benefits from full capital and current account convertibility under Eurozone Treaty rules (TFEU Articles 63–65). There are no exchange controls on current-account trade settlements, intercompany financing, dividends, or liquidation proceeds, and no requirement for prior central-bank approval of EUR or foreign-currency transactions. The practical constraints are: (i) profit remittances cannot be made unless the French SARL has filed its tax returns and settled the corresponding corporate income tax and social liabilities, and only to the extent distributable reserves exist after the legal reserve (5% of share capital up to 10%) is constituted; (ii) dividend distributions to a non-resident parent are subject to a 30% domestic withholding tax that may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty (e.g., France–China DTA for a corporate parent holding at least 10% of the SARL's share capital, subject to treaty-look-through and substance conditions); (iii) Eurozone monetary integration implies that the euro is fully convertible, but foreign-currency flows remain subject to Banque de France statistical reporting obligations under the balance-of-payments (BOP) framework, including a monthly declaration where a client's cumulative foreign exchange transactions exceed the relevant notification thresholds. The SARL's functional currency is the euro; USD/CNY balances should be held only as strictly cash tiers within the liquidity waterfall and not as structural investments to avoid FX translation volatility under the ANSF (Règlement ANC n°2016-07) recognition rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion ratio applies in France or the Eurozone. The SARL may freely hold, use, or reinvest 100% of its export proceeds in EUR or any foreign currency. The only legally binding obligations are statistical and documentary: (a) any settlement with a non-resident counterparty reaching or exceeding EUR 15,000 per transaction must be reported to the Banque de France through the authorized intermediary bank; (b) when cumulative monthly settlements with the same non-resident counterparty exceed EUR 50,000, the bank must file a consolidated BOP declaration (capitulatif des opérations de change); (c) a resident entity crossing cumulative foreign-currency flows of EUR 15 million in a month must itself file the relevant BOP return through its bank; and (d) original trade documentation (commercial invoices, SWIFT MT103 records, transport documents, customs SAD/Intrastat evidence) must be retained for at least five years under Articles L.123-22 and L.123-23 of the French Commercial Code. No foreign-currency account authorization from ACPR is necessary beyond standard banking facility documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) + Multi-Currency Operational Concentration Account (EUR/USD/CNY)
Operational Current Account + Dedicated SWIFT/LC Trade Finance Facility (Dailly / CREDOC)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (CACIB) / Crédit Agricole LCL
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account + FX Hedging Line (change à terme, swaps) with USD clearing sweep

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial, member of Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account + Confirming Bank seat for UCP 600 import/export LCs
Multi-Currency Operational Account (EUR/USD/CNY/HKD) with Asia-corridor trade advisory and cross-border liquidity overlay
Operational Account only; commercially limited for trade finance and FX hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for operational EUR disbursements under approximately €100,000 per month and for routine SEPA flows; LOW-MEDIUM for capital escrow, trade finance, FX hedging, and inbound FDI routing. French-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2/EMD2 — including Qonto, Shine, N26 France, and Blank — offer accelerated remote onboarding, but they are legally incapable of: (i) granting credit, discounting commercial paper, or advancing trade funding (Article L.525-8 CMF); (ii) issuing an attestation de dépôt des fonds or capital-blocking certificate required for a SARL share-capital escrow (only a full-licensed credit institution can certify funds blocking under French corporate law); (iii) executing FX forwards, swaps, options, or NDFs, since these are MiFID II investment services requiring an investment-firm or credit-institution licence; (iv) submitting Banque de France BOP filings and DG Trésor FDI notifications directly. Post-Brexit, a UK-FCA-authorised EMI has no European passport into France and must obtain a French branch agreement from ACPR; consequently, the SARL should use EMIs solely as a disbursement automation layer beneath a primary tier-1 relationship, never as the sole banking rail for capital, FX, or letters of credit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under ACPR anti-money-laundering guidelines (2015-15, revised) and Articles L.561-5 and L.561-6 of the CMF, a mandatory first interview applies to (i) the gérant holding general management powers, (ii) each person with A or B signature rights on the account, and (iii) the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) as registered on the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE). For a foreign-controlled SARL, French tier-1 banks require the primary gérant to appear physically at a French branch with original identity documents, the certified parent board resolution appointing the gérant, and, unless the gérant is a French resident, either a notarised power of attorney (procuration authentique) or a sworn translation of the appointment deed. A live video interview may be accepted for silent partners or non-operational UBOs, but it is not accepted for the primary gérant by BNPP, Société Générale, CACIB, CIC, or HSBC Continental Europe in the absence of a pre-existing high-quality EU banking relationship and a formal reference letter from the referring bank. Remote-only onboarding is practically unavailable for a newly incorporated SARL in a manufacturing sector with cross-border LFP battery flows; the cost-effective alternative is to appoint a French-resident co-gérant or a local authorised representative (représentant légal) to complete the interview at the branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or significant shareholder chain located in a high-risk third country, a FATF-monitored jurisdiction, or a jurisdiction lacking adequate tax information exchange with France.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RNE-compliant UBO declaration; notarised and apostilled birth certificates of all natural-person UBOs; certified passport copies; sworn source-of-wealth declaration and source-of-funds file for each UBO (salary slips, audited accounts, asset-sale deeds, parent dividends); audited parent company financial statements for the last two years; six-month applicant bank statement evidencing the funding trail; a written UBO-continuity commitment and irrevocable authority to notify the bank of any UBO change under Article L.561-10 CMF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital injection structured as a shareholder current account (compte courant d'associé) rather than pure equity, or capital deposited from a non-resident parent trading as a multi-jurisdiction holding without clear corporate substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank attestation de dépôt des fonds issued by the credit institution; notarised deed of incorporation or extraordinary general assembly minutes approving the capital increase; certified copy of the intercompany shareholder loan agreement with commercial-rate interest benchmarked within the CGI Article 212 safe harbor; proof of corporate substance (registered address, employees, board minutes, tax-filing receipts) of the lending parent; confirmation that the current-account balance stays within the 150:100 debt/equity thin-capitalisation ceiling to prevent recharacterisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow inconsistency between declared ISIC 2720 battery-pack assembly activity and rapid pass-through transactions involving commodity-trading intermediaries, shell trading desks, or unscreened Asian procurement agents for LFP cathode powder, lithium carbonate, or cells.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transactional file per procurement: executed purchase order; final commercial invoice; Incoterms 2020 conditions; transport documents (bill of lading, CMR, AWB); French customs single administrative document (SAD) and Intrastat/Extrastat filings where applicable; product documentation (UN38.3 test summaries, MSDS, certificate of origin) confirming physical goods movement; a 24-month projected settlement pattern and counterparty list with LEIs; written confirmation that no crypto or virtual-asset corridors are or will be used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic exposure of battery-pack exports or procurements to jurisdictions subject to EU sanctions, dual-use controls, or French export-control restrictions (e.g., use in energy-storage projects with potential military end-use).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dual-use classification analysis under EU Regulation 2021/821 demonstrating non-classification or, if classified, a proper French Ministry of Economy export licence; customs clearance records with SAD numbers; ICC model end-user and end-use certificates; restricted-party screening results for all counterparties maintained at each payment date; DG Trésor authorization or no-objection letter if the activity falls within the critical-technology perimeter; copy of the trade-compliance manual and denial-order screening evidence held by the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and statutory-package mismatch: RNE business-object clause describing only 'solar/consulting services' while banking flows show battery manufacturing and large-value LC transactions, triggering beneficial-owner and business-description inconsistency alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended articles of association (statuts à jour) registered with the RNE stating full scope: 'conception, industrialisation, assemblage, import-export et négoce de systèmes de batteries lithium-fer-phosphate et composants connexes'; current RCS/Kbis extract; auditor's (commissaire aux comptes) certificate validating the statutary-activity alignment; ERP treasury-control file documenting two-signature rule, segregation of duties, payment waterfall, and vendor master controls; a signed management letter confirming that transactional flows strictly mirror the registered volet social.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound protocol: (1) Equity capital injection — the SARL opens a dedicated capital escrow (compte bloqué) with a licensed credit institution; the non-resident parent remits via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for EUR) with Field 70 declaring 'apport en capital social / augmentation de capital' and referencing the corporate resolution; the bank verifies the RNE UBO extract and issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds; funds are released to the operational account only after the deed is signed and registered with the Registre National des Entreprises. (2) Shareholder current account (compte courant d'associé) — funds may be credited directly to the operational account; the payment narrative must reference the signed intercompany loan agreement, and the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code '2300' (other investment loans/financing) must be transmitted to the bank; the interest rate and the 150% debt-to-equity thin-capitalisation ceiling must be reconciled before deposit to prevent partial disallowance under Article 212 CGI. (3) FDI screening — where the investing parent is established outside the EU and the French venture is poised to engage in energy storage or battery-related critical technologies, DG Trésor prior authorisation may be triggered under French FDI rules (Articles L.151-3 seq. CMF, evolutions by Decree 2023-1294); the SARL must ascertain the applicable perimeter and obtain either a prior clearance or a no-objection letter before the escrow is released; an ex-post ministerial declaration is insufficient for controlled entities. Verification on receipt: the bank matches the MT103 Field 70, the corporate resolution, the UBO register, and the bankinternal source-of-funds records; inbound transfers through third-country nominee or consolidation accounts are prohibited, as are crypto-bridge, cash-courier, and non-bank PSP credit structures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) EUR supplier runs are settled via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) on TARGET2, with SEPA Instant for sub-€100,000 urgent components; (ii) non-EUR disbursements (USD, CNY, HKD for LFP cathode powder, lithium carbonate, cells, busbars, and BMS boards) are executed by SWIFT MT103, with Field 70 containing the commercial invoice number, relevant HS codes (HS 8507.60 for LFP battery packs and cells; HS 8537.10 for battery management systems; HS 8507.60.00/HS 8506.80 for ancillary power equipment), and the ISIC-aligned payment narrative to satisfy Banque de France BOP matching and transaction monitoring; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600: import LCs issued via SWIFT MT700 and confirmed by CACIB, CIC, or Société Générale, available at sight for LFP cell purchases with a maximum tenor of 120 days from bill of lading, conditioned on full-set original bills of lading, signed commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and independent third-party inspection certificate (SGS/BV/Cotecna); export LCs may be transferred (MT720) upstream to the core cell supplier to compress the cash conversion cycle and to lock the financing margin; (iv) documentary collection (D/P, D/A) is permissible for mid-value spot purchases below LC thresholds; (v) every outbound transaction must be traceable from the ERP treasury ledger (X3/SAP or equivalent) to the SWIFT confirmation and customs SAD files; all settlement evidence is retained in a secured archive for five years under Article L.123-22 of the Commercial Code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (change à terme) — plain-vanilla deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/CNY forwards matched to confirmed purchase orders or receivables, generally up to 12 months tenor without ACPR pre-clearance.
FX Swap (swap de change) — short-term roll of maturity mismatches between intercompany shareholder advances and Chinese supplier payment dates, prudently limited to less than six months.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) — applicable where the SARL carries EUR-denominated capex debt against USD/CNY-denominated feedstock commitments and where the bank relationship supports ISDA 2002 CSA documentation.

NDF (Non-Deliverable Forward) — available only where the underlying invoice currency is non-convertible or has a restricted deliverable market, e.g. offshore RMB NDF, and where the trade exposure is fully evidenced; the bank will require a hedge-adequacy opinion to satisfy the MIFID II suitability/appropriateness assessment.

Plain-vanilla FX Options (EUR call / USD put, EUR put / CNY call) — legally permitted but recommended to be executed at the corporate-treasury level of the parent; the SARL must pass the bank's MIFID II appropriateness test and maintain a board-approved hedging policy (politique de couverture) describing permissible instruments, stop-loss limits, and tenor ceilings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting (AGOA) approving annual accounts and discharge to the managing director
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record — minutes recorded in the SARL's statutory decision register (no governmental filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (court-approved extension available)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On failure, any shareholder may petition the Commercial Court president to compel convocation under a per-day court fine (astreinte); the manager is exposed to a criminal fine of up to EUR 4,500 (Code de commerce, Art. L.241-5).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the INPI guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of AGOA approval and, in any case, within 7 months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order to file under coercive daily penalty (Art. L.232-23-4); public prosecutor referral; non-filing for two consecutive years may trigger judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RNE.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs; Crédit Impôt Recherche (CIR) equal to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100,000; Crédit Impôt Innovation (CII) 20% of eligible innovation expenditure; exemption for Jeunes Entreprises Innovantes (JEI) during first 8 profitable years; territorial reduced rate for capital gains on disposals of equity stakes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) and annexed schedules 2043-C, 2050 to 2059; mandatory electronic filing through the EFI module of impots.gouv.fr or EDI/SEP transmission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of fiscal year closing; for calendar-year taxpayers by 3 May (or next business day if the 3rd falls on a weekend or public holiday).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result before tax (profit or loss).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL subject to IS through a French permanent establishment: report the PE's French-source result only; foreign head-office income excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments and reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include recharacterised transfer-pricing adjustments and any add-backs required under Article 209 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net taxable profit before deduction of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reflect French PE separate accounts, including proper allocation of head-office expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year deficits eligible for carryforward under Article 209 CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deficit carryforward is limited to €1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable profit; non-resident PE shall compute on the same basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of current taxable result offset against carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only if the non-resident has an established French PE with historical losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Remaining operating deficit carried forward to future years after prior-year offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the 20-year carryforward ceiling and preserve supporting schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% surcharge on the assessed corporate tax, increased to 10% after a 30-day formal notice, 40% for bad faith, 80% for organised fraud; fixed penalty of €200 per missing or unfiled balance-sheet annex; monthly interest of 0.20% on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a treaty reduced rate, the French paying SARL must hold a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the beneficial owner's competent tax authority and submitted via Form 5001/5002/5003 (lightened withholding procedure) before the payment; for DTA claims applying to dividends under the OECD Model, the beneficial owner must hold at least 10-25% of the paying entity's capital (treaty-specific) and maintain real economic substance; alternatively, an annual refund claim may be filed with the French non-resident tax service (Service des impôts des particuliers non-résidents). Within the EU/EEA, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive is invoked by filing Form RF-5001 before the second transfer; a minimum 10% shareholding and two-year holding condition apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding: royalties on patents, trademarks, and copyrights paid to non-residents: 33.33%; interest on debt instruments: generally 0% (exempt under French domestic law), except profit-participating loans or payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions (30%). Treaty rates: typical DTA rates for royalties 0-10%; interest 0-15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when related-party transactions exceed €1,000,000 annual aggregate; Master File mandatory when the group's consolidated revenue reaches €750,000,000; all taxpayers above €400,000 revenue or assets are subject to simplified transfer-pricing documentation if related-party cross-border flows exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate an ESR-style registry, but the general anti-abuse rule (Article L.64 LPF), substance-over-form doctrine, and BEPS Principal Purpose Test require the French SARL to demonstrate adequate premises, operational personnel, local board decision-making, and control over LFP battery-pack assembly risk to obtain treaty benefits and avoid sham-company recharacterisation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating taxable profits in the Form 2065-SD by inflating intercompany recharge invoices, booking fictitious expenses, or recognising manufacturing revenue in an offshore zero-rate shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty: 40% of understated tax for bad faith; 80% for organised fraud; monthly 0.20% late interest; criminal fine up to €1,500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (7 years when organised fraud is established).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil joint liability for corporate tax under Article L.267 LPF; piercing of the corporate veil for abus de bien social; French travel ban, asset freeze, and up to 5 years' imprisonment for managers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a SARL without physical premises, employees, or board meetings in France while channelling battery pack profits through the French entity solely to access DTA treaty reductions and withholdings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under Article 45 CGI; disallowance of deductible expenses; denial of treaty relief under the Principal Purpose Test; reassessment for six years; penalty up to 80% of additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint liability for the entire reassessed tax and penalties; potential criminal tax-evasion convictions; personal travel restrictions and prohibition on managing any French company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving customer proceeds via Swift LC or TT wire without filing the French ‘Beneficiary Owner’ register (RBE), failing to identify ultimate beneficial owners, or executing cash transactions above €10,000 without AML due diligence in the LiFePO4 battery-pack trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to €1,000,000; sanctions up to 10% of consolidated turnover for breaches of the French Monetary and Financial Code; suspension of corporate registration; penalties for failure to file RBE declarations up to €750,000 for legal entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment up to 5 years for money-laundering facilitation, professional disqualification, international asset-freezing orders, and potential seizure of shares in the French SARL.
